newsitem.title: KYRGYZSTAN: Newmont, Santa Fe Pacific sign Kyrgyz gold deal.
newsitem.headline: Newmont, Santa Fe Pacific sign Kyrgyz gold deal.

text.p: U.S. gold majors Newmont Mining Corp and Santa Fe Pacific Gold Corp signed a joint venture with Kyrgyzstan on Thursday to explore the former Soviet republic's Solton-Sary gold deposit.

"The creation of this joint venture is among the largest geological surveys in Kyrgyzstan and possibly in the Commonwealth of Independent States," Dastan Sarygulov, head of state gold concern Kyrgyzaltyn, told a news conference.

He said the deposit could be second in size to the republic's Kumtor field which, with reserves of around 288 tonnes of gold, is being mined by Canada's Cameco Corp in a joint venture with Kyrgyzaltyn.
Sarygulov gave no details of reserves for Solton-Sary.
Newmont and Santa Fe Pacific will spend 30 million soms on exploring the field.
If the two companies find gold, they have the exclusive right to to mine Solton-Sary. The companies, which plan to merge next month, also have the right to freely export production.
Newmont is already producing around 12 tonnes of gold a year in neighbouring Uzbekistan. ($1 = 17.9 soms)
